instruction: Change the sender name in your Thunderbird email account to 'Dr. Smith' to appear on outgoing messages.

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting a custom display name (sender name) for the email account. The evaluator checks the mail.identity.id1.fullName preference in prefs.js to verify it is set to 'Dr. Smith'. Uses the existing check_thunderbird_prefs metric function.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checks if mail.identity.id1.fullName preference is set to 'Dr. Smith'
Complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (set display name), evaluator checks exactly this requirement
Correct data flow: get_vm_file extracts prefs.js from VM, check_thunderbird_prefs parses and validates the preference value

Metric function correctly handles expected parameter: when expected.type='rule', the metric receives rules dict directly (via get_rule) and correctly accesses rule.get('expect', {}) and rule.get('unexpect', {})
Appropriate postconfig: closes Thunderbird window to ensure preferences are flushed to disk before reading prefs.js
Edge cases handled: metric returns 0.0 when result is None, handles missing preferences gracefully
Type compatibility is correct: get_vm_file with multi=False returns str or None, which check_thunderbird_prefs handles properly (static warning is false positive)
Expected value is semantically correct: mail.identity.id1.fullName is the correct Thunderbird preference for email display name

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_thunderbird_prefs first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
